- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap next-day forecast at +5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment drops sharply (≤0.3) followed by a price drop, model underreacts; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% to match sentiment shift.
- Model frequently overestimates mid-term (10–20 day) trends; apply mean reversion bias: if forecast > true outcome by >3%, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is low and price is falling, model often fails to anticipate further decline; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast if sentiment <0.4 and price <70.
- Forecast horizon 30d often exhibits lag: true price often dips 1–3 days after model peak; adjust forecast to lag 1–2 days if sentiment is neutral or declining.
